\chapter{Nine Doorway Forms}
\label{ch:gu-doorway-forms}
\hlchaptermodality{3}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can read and write nine Gujarati forms needed by the next conversations: \gu{જ}, \gu{ો}, \gu{ં}, \gu{ી}, \gu{ુ}, \gu{છ}, \gu{ક}, \gu{ણ}, and \gu{શ}.}

With every model covered, identify the nine doorway forms and write them from spoken sound or role cues, earning separate reading and writing scores.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[ja]{\gu{જ} — the consonant ja}

\label{lesson:GU-W03-ja}



\begin{quote}
Without looking back, say the leave-taking word aavjo once. Today you meet the letter at its centre.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Script — meet one form}
Keep \textbf{\gu{જ}} visible. It is the consonant ja, pronounced \emph{ja}. Begin near the upper left and circle the small upper-left loop. Continue diagonally through the crossing body, circle the lower-right loop, and sweep into the long upper-right exit without lifting.

\subsection*{Writing — notice and trace}
Finger-trace \textbf{\gu{જ}} once, then air-trace it once. Notice two loops joined through a crossing; no pen lift.

\subsection*{Writing — copy with the model}
Copy visible \textbf{\gu{જ}} once. Compare only the landmark named above and repair it once if needed.

\subsection*{Writing — recall after hiding}
Hide the model and write \emph{ja} once. Uncover \textbf{\gu{જ}}, compare, and stop after one repair.

\section[-o]{\gu{ો} — the attached vowel sign o}

\label{lesson:GU-W03-o-matra}



\begin{quote}
Hide the model from the previous lesson and write ja once. Check only its two loops.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Script — meet one form}
Keep \textbf{\gu{ો}} visible. It is the attached vowel sign o, pronounced \emph{-o}. This is the vowel sign o: the long-aa bar on the right plus a short mark above. It attaches to a consonant and replaces that consonant's inherent a.

\subsection*{Writing — notice and trace}
Finger-trace \textbf{\gu{ો}} once, then air-trace it once. Notice right-side bar plus high mark; one attached right bar and one high mark.

\subsection*{Writing — copy with the model}
Copy visible \textbf{\gu{ો}} once. Compare only the landmark named above and repair it once if needed.

\subsection*{Writing — recall after hiding}
Hide the model and write \emph{-o} once. Uncover \textbf{\gu{ો}}, compare, and stop after one repair.

\section[ṃ]{\gu{ં} — the nasal mark anusvara}

\label{lesson:GU-W03-anusvara}



\begin{quote}
Write the attached o sign once from memory. Check the right bar, then the mark above.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Script — meet one form}
Keep \textbf{\gu{ં}} visible. It is the nasal mark anusvara, pronounced \emph{ṃ}. This is anusvāra, a single dot above the syllable. It marks nasal sound; it is small, but its position above the writing line is part of the spelling.

\subsection*{Writing — notice and trace}
Finger-trace \textbf{\gu{ં}} once, then air-trace it once. Notice a single high dot; one dot placed above.

\subsection*{Writing — copy with the model}
Copy visible \textbf{\gu{ં}} once. Compare only the landmark named above and repair it once if needed.

\subsection*{Writing — recall after hiding}
Hide the model and write \emph{ṃ} once. Uncover \textbf{\gu{ં}}, compare, and stop after one repair.

\section[-ī]{\gu{ી} — the attached long-i vowel sign}

\label{lesson:GU-W03-ii-matra}



\begin{quote}
Place the nasal dot once from memory. Keep it above the writing line.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Script — meet one form}
Keep \textbf{\gu{ી}} visible. It is the attached long-i vowel sign, pronounced \emph{-ī}. This is the long-ī vowel sign. It attaches to the right of a consonant as an upright curl with a trailing tail, replacing the inherent a with long ī.

\subsection*{Writing — notice and trace}
Finger-trace \textbf{\gu{ી}} once, then air-trace it once. Notice right-side curl with a tail; one attached curl and tail.

\subsection*{Writing — copy with the model}
Copy visible \textbf{\gu{ી}} once. Compare only the landmark named above and repair it once if needed.

\subsection*{Writing — recall after hiding}
Hide the model and write \emph{-ī} once. Uncover \textbf{\gu{ી}}, compare, and stop after one repair.

\section[-u]{\gu{ુ} — the attached short-u vowel sign}

\label{lesson:GU-W03-u-matra}



\begin{quote}
Write the long-ī sign once from memory. Check that its curl sits to the right.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Script — meet one form}
Keep \textbf{\gu{ુ}} visible. It is the attached short-u vowel sign, pronounced \emph{-u}. This is the short-u vowel sign. It hangs below its consonant as a small hook. The position below, not beside or above, identifies the mark.

\subsection*{Writing — notice and trace}
Finger-trace \textbf{\gu{ુ}} once, then air-trace it once. Notice a below-letter hook; one small hook below.

\subsection*{Writing — copy with the model}
Copy visible \textbf{\gu{ુ}} once. Compare only the landmark named above and repair it once if needed.

\subsection*{Writing — recall after hiding}
Hide the model and write \emph{-u} once. Uncover \textbf{\gu{ુ}}, compare, and stop after one repair.

\section[chha]{\gu{છ} — the consonant chha}

\label{lesson:GU-W03-chha}



\begin{quote}
Write the below-letter u hook once from memory. Keep it compact.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Script — meet one form}
Keep \textbf{\gu{છ}} visible. It is the consonant chha, pronounced \emph{chha}. Begin near the upper left and circle the upper-left lobe. Continue through the middle and around the broad lower body, then climb the outer right curve and circle the upper-right lobe without lifting.

\subsection*{Writing — notice and trace}
Finger-trace \textbf{\gu{છ}} once, then air-trace it once. Notice two high lobes around a broad lower body; no pen lift.

\subsection*{Writing — copy with the model}
Copy visible \textbf{\gu{છ}} once. Compare only the landmark named above and repair it once if needed.

\subsection*{Writing — recall after hiding}
Hide the model and write \emph{chha} once. Uncover \textbf{\gu{છ}}, compare, and stop after one repair.

\section[ka]{\gu{ક} — the consonant ka}

\label{lesson:GU-W03-ka}



\begin{quote}
Write chha once from memory. Check the two upper lobes before looking back.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Script — meet one form}
Keep \textbf{\gu{ક}} visible. It is the consonant ka, pronounced \emph{ka}. Begin at the upper right, circle the upper loop, and continue diagonally through the rounded lower body. Lift once; sweep the separate diagonal cross-stroke from lower left to upper right.

\subsection*{Writing — notice and trace}
Finger-trace \textbf{\gu{ક}} once, then air-trace it once. Notice looped body plus a separate rising cross-stroke; one pen lift.

\subsection*{Writing — copy with the model}
Copy visible \textbf{\gu{ક}} once. Compare only the landmark named above and repair it once if needed.

\subsection*{Writing — recall after hiding}
Hide the model and write \emph{ka} once. Uncover \textbf{\gu{ક}}, compare, and stop after one repair.

\section[ṇa]{\gu{ણ} — the retroflex consonant nna}

\label{lesson:GU-W03-nna}



\begin{quote}
Write ka once from memory: body first, then the separate rising cross-stroke.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Script — meet one form}
Keep \textbf{\gu{ણ}} visible. It is the retroflex consonant nna, pronounced \emph{ṇa}. Descend the left spine and sweep through its hooked lower tail. Lift and circle the separate middle bowl. Lift again, descend the tall right spine, and turn through its lower foot.

\subsection*{Writing — notice and trace}
Finger-trace \textbf{\gu{ણ}} once, then air-trace it once. Notice left hook, middle bowl, right spine; two pen lifts.

\subsection*{Writing — copy with the model}
Copy visible \textbf{\gu{ણ}} once. Compare only the landmark named above and repair it once if needed.

\subsection*{Writing — recall after hiding}
Hide the model and write \emph{ṇa} once. Uncover \textbf{\gu{ણ}}, compare, and stop after one repair.

\section[sha]{\gu{શ} — the consonant sha}

\label{lesson:GU-W03-sha}



\begin{quote}
Write retroflex nna once from memory. Check the left hook, middle bowl, and right spine.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Script — meet one form}
Keep \textbf{\gu{શ}} visible. It is the consonant sha, pronounced \emph{sha}. Begin at the upper right, circle the small upper loop, and continue through the broad lower body into its tail. Lift once; descend the tall right spine and turn through its lower foot.

\subsection*{Writing — notice and trace}
Finger-trace \textbf{\gu{શ}} once, then air-trace it once. Notice small upper loop, broad body, separate right spine; one pen lift.

\subsection*{Writing — copy with the model}
Copy visible \textbf{\gu{શ}} once. Compare only the landmark named above and repair it once if needed.

\subsection*{Writing — recall after hiding}
Hide the model and write \emph{sha} once. Uncover \textbf{\gu{શ}}, compare, and stop after one repair.
